signals.title: JPY/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: The G10 currency scorecard shows JPY leading with a 1W average of +1.281% across 7 pairs, while NOK lags at −0.907% across 2 pairs, generating an extreme 2.187% bilateral spread. JPY strength dominates the board despite BoJ 1.25% holding a 325bp policy rate deficit against Norges Bank 4.5%. Spot USD/NOK sits at 9.592, holding cleanly above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 9.375/9.427/9.565, confirming broad krone vulnerability. Leveraged funds JPY net positioning sits at +4,472 contracts (pctl 98, z +2.66), reflecting crowded bullish positioning that is outperforming rate differentials. This severe bilateral divergence signals structural liquidation of high-carry funding trades across Scandies into yen. Trade bias: Bullish JPY/NOK; wide performance gap favors persistence despite carry headwind. Catalyst: BoJ Summary of Opinions release at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Reversal of cross-asset deleveraging compresses the 2.187% performance spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Corridors + Options Put Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.41, positioned above SMA20 at 156.13 but contained below its SMA50/200 resistance band at 158.38/158.46. Headlines regarding US administration statements on control over the Strait of Hormuz layer geopolitical risk directly onto primary energy-importing currencies. A 267bp OIS carry advantage favors USD via SOFR 3.90% against TONA 1.23%, sustaining base support for the pair. However, the options market exhibits significant caution: 25d risk reversals print at −2.60 alongside an ATM implied vol of 9.1% versus 30-day realized volatility of 10.1% (VRP −1.1%). This pronounced put skew indicates that desks are actively paying up for downside put protection despite the underlying nominal rate spread. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-supported while holding above 156.13. Catalyst: Japan Tokyo Core CPI print at 23:30 UTC. Risk: Escalation in regional energy chokepoints triggers an aggressive flight to safe assets and a breach below SMA20 at 156.13.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Rates Driver + Technical Breakdown
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1333, trading firmly below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.1514/1.1536/1.1620 following a 2.78% monthly decline. Policy rate differentials anchor the downside, with Fed 4.00% (HIKING) maintaining a 135bp nominal premium over ECB 2.65% (HIKING), mirrored by a +146bp OIS spread favoring SOFR over €STR. US 5Y yields rose +23bp over 5D (FRED, as of Sep 28) composed entirely of real yield +23bp and breakeven +0bp, showing real-yield-led rate momentum behind the dollar. While German inflation accelerated to 2-year highs, CFTC Leveraged Funds EUR net short widened by −7,450 contracts WoW to −58,805 contracts (pctl 19, z −1.01), confirming institutional selling into euro rallies. The combination of restrictive US real rates and broken multi-month technical moving averages maintains heavy topside supply. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, constrained below moving average clusters. Catalyst: Euro Area CPI y/y release at 09:00 UTC. Risk: Euro Area headline inflation accelerates significantly above 3.0% forecast, forcing an aggressive hawkish repricing in the ECB curve.

signals.title: NZD/USD — Positioning + Technical Alignment
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5635, hovering below its SMA20/50/200 overhead band at 0.5764/0.5836/0.5852 after sliding 5.38% over the past month. The policy spread strongly favors the greenback, with Fed 4.00% offering a 125bp carry premium over RBNZ 2.75%. Leveraged Funds expanded net shorts by −2,897 contracts WoW to −5,216 contracts, while commercial accounts added +13,986 contracts to Dealer net shorts. Retail positioning registers an extreme reading with 92% of traders long, running counter to the prevailing multi-week downtrend. This severe positioning skew leaves retail longs vulnerable to forced liquidation on marginal new lows. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD, trend continuation aligned with technical moving averages. Catalyst: US ISM Manufacturing PMI release at 14:00 UTC. Risk: Spot recovery and daily close above the SMA20 anchor at 0.5764.
